title: Round 3 / ECDLP-8: literature and exact bound for mixed character sums along EC subgroups
question: What is the exact, sourced statement of the best Weil-type bound for sums sum_{Q in E(F_p)} psi(Q) chi(g(Q)) (psi a group character of E(F_p), chi a multiplicative character, g a rational function), including constants and degree dependence, and what is known about the limiting distribution (Katz/Deligne equidistribution) of the normalized sums? Does it explain a periodogram variance below 1 for chi(x([k]P))?

sources.title: Kohel, Shparlinski - On Exponential Sums and Group Generators for Elliptic Curves over Finite Fields (ANTS 2000, LNCS 1838, 395-404; authors' preprint; additive-character sums S(omega,psi,f))
Perel'muter - Estimation of a sum along an algebraic curve, Mat. Zametki 5 (1969) 373-380 (index record, abstract only)
Merai - Construction of pseudorandom binary sequences over elliptic curves using multiplicative characters, Publ. Math. Debrecen 80 (2012) 199-213
Beelen, Doumen - Pseudorandom sequences from elliptic curves (Oaxaca 2001, Springer 2002, 37-52), bibliographic record only
Ahmadi, Shparlinski - Bilinear character sums and sum-product problems on elliptic curves (arXiv 1302.4210), bibliography only

claims: Verified literature: Kohel-Shparlinski (ANTS 2000) bound |S(omega,psi,f)| <= 2 deg(f) sqrt(q) concerns ADDITIVE psi(f(P)); the multiplicative mixed sum S(omega,chi,f) is treated by Perel'muter 1969, Perret 1991, Beelen-Doumen 2002, Merai 2012 (Lemma 1, incomplete sums, factor 1+log N, f not a d-th power). Explicit constants for the multiplicative case were not read in primary sources.

Derived (from Weil/Bombieri L-functions as quoted in Kohel-Shparlinski): |S(omega,chi,g)+eps| <= D sqrt(p), D = degree of the ramified support of div(g) (D=2 for g=x,x+1,2x; 4 for x^2+x+1,y; 6 for xy); checked numerically, no violation, D=2 bound essentially sharp.

Proved identities: sum_c |F(c)|^2 = rN (mean of periodogram is exactly ~1) and sum_c |F(c)|^4 = r sum_R |A(R)|^2 with A the cyclic autocorrelation of chi(g(.)); full-range sums are exact group-character sums for r prime.
Half-range DFT: completion gives only O(D sqrt(p) log p), i.e. normalized O(D^2 log^2 p); vacuous for the variance anomaly.

Heuristic (not proved, no source found): F(c)/sqrt(N) for g=x is Sato-Tate/semicircle (SU(2)): E u^4 = 2, var(full-range periodogram) = 1, and half-range periodogram variance = 1 + kappa/3 = 2/3, matching the observed 0.66; for symmetric D=4 g it behaves as USp(4): E u^4 = 3, half-range var 1. Pooled 115k values: moments 1, 1.995, 4.981 vs 1, 2, 5; KS 0.004. g=y is empirically SU(2)-like although D=4 (unexplained).

No information about the discrete log follows; Weil bound limits every Fourier correlation to about D/sqrt(p). A leak would require a non-negligible computable distinguisher of k-classes from Q=[k]P (stated in report).
next_action: Reviewer: (1) check claim (C) conductor count against Perel'muter/Perret theorem texts; (2) test p up to ~1e5 with FFT for g=x vs y vs x^2+x+1 (E u^4 = 2, 2, 3) and resolve why g=y is SU(2)-like; (3) try a decisive test of the 1+kappa/3 half-range law with other D (e.g. cubic g, order-4 chi); (4) set HYP-242da418 to reflect that the claimed 'non-Exp(1) bounded law' is supported but that C(d) must be the conductor degree D, not 2deg g, and that the mechanism needs a source or proof.
